articles.title: Brands are all in on creators. Meanwhile in reality, the economics crash
articles.summary: US brand spend on influencer marketing keeps climbing, but the industry's own numbers are questionable. Its $5.78 return per $1 spent is earned media value, not real revenue, based on estimated impressions and rate cards. A third of followers on the average creator account show signs of being fake or purchased, while more than half of creators earn under $15,000 a year. As brands shift toward nano-creators, Americans are also posting less than they did five years ago. What's left is a reach channel, not the trust economy it promised.

articles.title: Spotify's new ‘skip' button could end the podcast business as we know it
articles.summary: Spotify is testing a feature that lets some Premium users skip podcast ads, promotions, and filler, raising concerns among publishers that rely on direct-sold ads. The move could weaken podcast ad revenue as audiences increasingly shift toward YouTube and video. Spotify says the feature could keep listeners engaged longer, but publishers worry that easier ad skipping could make their inventory less valuable.

articles.title: Clay's “AI Writing Policy”
articles.summary: Clay's new AI writing policy requires employees to fully own AI-assisted writing, treating writing as a way to develop understanding rather than bypass thinking. It also discourages generating long documents from short prompts, asking writers to respect readers' time and cut unnecessary AI-generated filler.

articles.title: Emotion-Led Ads Cut Costs 30%
articles.summary: A hop-infused tea brand initially focused its ads on being non-alcoholic, but customer research showed that belonging mattered more. It reframed the messaging around keeping the taste and social experience of beer without alcohol, lowering acquisition costs by 30% in two weeks. The approach also challenges excessive personalization, which can raise ad costs by narrowing audiences around individual profiles instead of broader emotional motivations.

articles.title: How to grow your AI Visibility with community signals
articles.summary: Community platforms act as a foundation for AI visibility across the funnel. Reddit, Wikipedia, and LinkedIn account for 99% of UGC citations in SaaS-related ChatGPT answers, while UGC sites hold 15-18% of non-vendor cited domains throughout the journey, more than 4X publishers' 4% share. Named authors and reps also tend to outperform brand accounts because communities treat people as participants rather than advertisers.

articles.title: Creators Aren't Just Making Content Anymore (Webinar)
articles.summary: On August 27, ADWEEK CEO Will Lee will moderate a conversation with Jayde I. Powell, Founder & Head of Creative at The Em Dash Co., about how creators are evolving beyond content into businesses. The session will explore community as a brand strategy and how creators are building products and owned distribution.

articles.title: How to run ChatGPT ads: A step-by-step guide from early campaigns
articles.summary: ChatGPT Ads are still early, so advertisers need to approach them as a testing ground. Start by confirming eligibility and setting up your account, then build campaigns and use context hints to reach relevant conversations instead of relying on keywords. Create your ads and install conversion tracking before launch. Once live, focus on testing creative and campaign structure since reporting offers limited insight into which conversations drive performance.

articles.title: How Three Product Marketing Leaders Set Up Their AI Workflows
articles.summary: AI workflows work best when they're built around how a company actually works, not copied from generic Skills or prompts. Three PMM leaders use connectors, reusable Skills, and company context in different ways. Mara Taylor uses AI to cut context switching, Natalie Marcotullio systematizes recurring marketing work, and Mike Hetrick builds guardrails for quality. Start with a repeatable task, test it on real work, add human checks, then refine it.

articles.title: How to Create Viral Ads ft. Harmon Brothers
articles.summary: Harmon Brothers makes viral ads by building every creative decision around the sale. It starts by deeply understanding the product, then turns awkward or unsexy problems into entertaining stories that explain the product and reduce purchase friction. Its ads hook viewers within the first 5 seconds and test multiple variations before scaling spend. Longer 3-6 minute videos help build purchase intent.

articles.title: MrBeast Hired a Head of TikTok. The Strategy Is Already Producing Records
articles.summary: Platform-specific creative teams could become the next stage of social strategy. MrBeast created a dedicated TikTok team led by a Head of TikTok and specialized creative talent to develop content for the platform. One of its first successes was a simple dance video that became TikTok's most reposted video ever. The result shows how content built for a specific platform can outperform content adapted from other channels, even with simpler production.

articles.title: How to get high intent Google Ad clicks
articles.summary: Use disqualifying ad copy to filter out low-intent clicks.

articles.summary: Google is testing a more AI-focused version of its homepage for people who aren't signed into a Google Account.
